changes.after: The revised conclusion presents the extracted subgraph as evidence for human judgment. False alarms can increase review burden, while omitted evidence can conceal a risk. The source-case evaluation measures false alarms, and endpoint recall and expert-reference coverage assess missing evidence. The Limitations section addresses dependence on the backbone and graph construction, together with the need for broader natural-case and end-to-end evaluation. The new Ethical Considerations section specifies human verification and advises against using outputs as the sole basis for consequential decisions. It also clarifies that injected conflicts are constructed evaluation cases, not factual claims about named entities or evidence of those conflicts in the original documents.
